hero.title: Oil Surges Above $107 as Middle East Crisis Deepens
hero.description: Rising attacks on energy infrastructure and growing pressure around major shipping routes are pushing oil prices higher and increasing concerns about inflation and global energy security.

breaking: 🚨 Brent crude rises to around $107.81 as Middle East tensions intensify.
🛢️ Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline remains shut after a drone attack, threatening a major alternative route for crude exports.
⚠️ Disruption to Saudi oil infrastructure could affect a significant share of global supply if the outage continues.
🚢 Shipping risks remain high around the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb.
🇸🇪 Sweden's centre-left opposition bloc is narrowly ahead in preliminary election results, but the final result is still being counted.
🇺🇦 A Russian drone struck a passenger train near Ukraine's border with Poland; no casualties were reported.
🇳🇬 Dangote Refinery has launched what Reuters describes as Africa's largest IPO to date.
💰 Dangote is offering 4.1 billion shares at ₦525 each, with the offering potentially raising more if oversubscribed.
🌍 Dangote plans to use the capital-market opportunity to support expansion of the refinery from 700,000 to 1.4 million barrels per day.
💻 Technology shares fall as leading AI executives call for a slower pace of AI development amid safety and investment concerns.

featured.title: Global Energy Shock Intensifies as Oil Passes $107
featured.content: Global energy markets are under renewed pressure as attacks affecting Saudi infrastructure coincide with continuing risks around the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, designed to provide an alternative route for transporting crude around Hormuz, has been temporarily shut. Meanwhile, higher tanker costs and shipping risks are adding to concerns about fuel prices, inflation and economic growth.

articles.title: Oil Markets Face Renewed Supply Pressure
articles.content: Brent crude rose to around $107.81 while US crude climbed to about $102.94 as investors assessed the growing risks to Middle Eastern energy infrastructure and shipping. The Saudi East-West pipeline shutdown is particularly important because it provides an alternative route for moving crude without relying entirely on the Strait of Hormuz. A prolonged disruption could increase pressure on fuel markets and inflation worldwide.
articles.imageQuery: Brent crude oil price tanker Saudi Arabia

articles.title: Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb Remain Major Shipping Risks
articles.content: The Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb remain central to the global energy crisis. Threats to vessels and disruption around the two strategic waterways are increasing transport costs and making energy shipments more difficult. The postponement of planned diplomatic discussions between Iran and Gulf states has also added uncertainty over the prospects for a quick reduction in maritime tensions.
articles.imageQuery: Strait of Hormuz cargo ships Bab el Mandeb shipping

articles.title: Dangote Refinery IPO Opens in Nigeria
articles.content: Dangote Petroleum Refinery has launched its initial public offering, offering 4.1 billion shares at ₦525 per share. Reuters reports that the offering could raise up to about $2.1 billion if it is fully subscribed and the additional greenshoe option is exercised. The IPO runs until 13 October and gives retail and institutional investors an opportunity to participate in one of Nigeria's most significant industrial assets.

articles.title: Dangote Targets Major Refinery Expansion
articles.content: The Dangote refinery currently has a stated capacity of 700,000 barrels per day. The company plans to expand that capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day by 2029. The expansion comes as Nigeria and other African economies face renewed concerns about fuel security, international crude prices and disruptions to global energy supply.

articles.title: Sweden Centre-Left Narrowly Ahead After Election
articles.content: Sweden's centre-left opposition bloc is narrowly ahead following Sunday's parliamentary election. Preliminary figures reported by Reuters put the bloc on course for around 176 seats in the 349-seat parliament, compared with 173 for the right-wing bloc led by Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson. The result remains preliminary. Sweden's final vote count began on Monday and is expected to take about a week, while negotiations will determine who can ultimately form a government.

articles.title: Ukraine Conflict Reaches Closer to Poland Border
articles.content: The war in Ukraine continues to create security concerns across Europe. A Russian drone struck a passenger train close to Ukraine's border with NATO member Poland on Sunday. The train was hit around two kilometres from the Polish border, but no casualties were reported. The incident has increased concern about the risks to transport infrastructure and the potential for the conflict to create further security pressure along NATO's eastern frontier.
articles.imageQuery: Ukraine Poland border railway train war

articles.title: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Remains a Major Health Concern
articles.content: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo remains an important public-health concern, with cases and deaths reported across several provinces. Health authorities and international partners continue surveillance, vaccination and response activities. The situation requires close monitoring because Ebola can spread rapidly when detection and isolation are delayed.
articles.imageQuery: Ebola health workers Democratic Republic Congo

articles.title: AI Warnings Trigger Fresh Technology Stock Sell-Off
articles.content: Technology markets came under pressure on Monday after leading artificial intelligence executives called for a slower pace of development because of growing safety concerns. AI-heavy stocks fell sharply in several Asian markets, adding to investor concerns about whether the enormous spending on chips, data centres and AI infrastructure can generate sufficient long-term returns.

articles.title: Energy Prices Put Central Banks Under Fresh Pressure
articles.content: Higher oil prices are creating a difficult policy environment for central banks. More expensive energy can raise transportation and production costs and eventually feed into consumer prices. At the same time, higher interest rates can slow economic growth. Policymakers therefore face a difficult balance between controlling inflation and avoiding unnecessary damage to economic activity.
articles.imageQuery: global financial markets inflation oil prices

articles.title: Asian Markets React to Oil and AI Concerns
articles.content: Asian financial markets faced renewed pressure as investors responded to higher oil prices, geopolitical uncertainty and a sharp decline in several AI-related technology shares. The combination of energy inflation and uncertainty around the profitability of large AI investments has increased caution among investors.

morningSummary: Good afternoon. Global energy markets are again under pressure as oil prices rise above $107 and Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline remains shut following a drone attack. Shipping risks around the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb continue to affect the outlook for global energy supplies. In Nigeria, the Dangote Refinery IPO has officially opened, creating a major opportunity for investors to participate in one of Africa's largest industrial assets. In Europe, Sweden's centre-left opposition is narrowly ahead after Sunday's election, while the final count continues. In Ukraine, a Russian drone struck a passenger train close to the Polish border without reported casualties. Technology markets are also under pressure following renewed concerns about the pace and risks of artificial intelligence development.
bigQuestion: If major energy and shipping routes remain disrupted for weeks, how much higher could fuel, transport, food and household costs become around the world?
